paper.central_claim: ACE treats contexts as evolving playbooks updated by a modular Generator-Reflector-Curator process with incremental delta updates and grow-and-refine, preventing brevity bias and context collapse; it improves agents (+10.6%) and domain tasks (+8.6%), works without labels using execution feedback, and lowers adaptation latency and rollout cost.

signatures.object: Playbook: itemized bullets (id, helpful/harmful counters, content) forming the agent/system context
signatures.information: Generator trajectories with execution outcomes (AppWorld) or ground-truth labels (labelled rows) available to the Reflector; Generator marks which bullets helped or misled
signatures.operation: Reflector (up to 5 refinement rounds) extracts lessons; Curator emits delta bullets; deterministic non-LLM merge + embedding dedup + lazy pruning
signatures.output: Updated playbook injected into the Generator's context
signatures.conditions: Offline: train split, up to 5 epochs; online: per-sample update on test stream; batch size 1
signatures.feedback: Execution success/failure or GT labels; without them finance online degrades
signatures.selection_rule: No validation-time acceptance test (unlike GEPA's 57-query validation); dedup threshold and pruning length trigger only
signatures.later_use: Always in the Generator's context at evaluation
signatures.claimed_effect: AppWorld +12.7..+17.1 avg; FiNER/Formula +7.5..+12.8 (with labels); removing delta updates cuts AppWorld gain from +17.0 to +3.6
signatures.failure_boundary: Weak reflector, noisy/no feedback, tasks needing concise instructions; harmful reflections every step push below base

gap.author_gap: Context adaptation methods suffer from brevity bias (prompt optimizers like GEPA) and context collapse (monolithic LLM rewriting such as Dynamic Cheatsheet).
gap.checked_gap: Supported against DC (collapse case with token counts) and GEPA (brevity); collapse evidence is one DC run, and incremental/itemized memories (A-MEM, AWM, Mem0-style) are discussed but not run.
gap.lineage: Reflexion/TextGrad/GEPA (prompt evolution) and Dynamic Cheatsheet (test-time cheatsheet) -> ACE (itemized deltas + Reflector + grow-and-refine).
gap.residue: Detail loss under repeated LLM rewriting; heuristics dropped by concise prompt optimizers.
gap.stakes: AppWorld accuracy drops from 66.7 to 57.1 in the DC collapse case; long-horizon agents depend on retained tool rules.
gap.method_response: Localized deltas merged deterministically, separate Reflector, dedup and lazy pruning.
gap.remaining_gap: No admission gate or utility-based retirement; reliance on feedback quality; higher serving input tokens.
unresolved: Whether A-MEM/AWM-style incremental stores also avoid collapse (not pinned locally)

rs_pattern.reason: son55 adopted. Conditioning a frozen model on an evolving playbook is the main move; C03 is not assigned under the run convention (no category holdout: offline is an instance split of the same benchmark, no cross-domain playbook transfer). Many-shot ICL is a simpler-conditioning control but does not substitute for the holdout. The load-bearing, ablated innovation — LLM-written itemized deltas merged by deterministic non-LLM logic (Table 18) — is the C25 move of confining the LLM to extraction/interfacing and offloading structured bookkeeping to exact code (partial: no verifier closes the loop).
